info.title: myrtle.moe API
info.description:
The public HTTP API behind [myrtle.moe](https://myrtle.moe), an Arknights companion app.

Every endpoint lives under `/api`. Responses are JSON unless noted; errors share a single envelope whose `error.code` is the stable field to branch on.

This document is generated from the server's own route definitions, so it describes what the running server actually serves: a route and its OpenAPI operation are the same declaration, and a test refuses any route that lacks one. If an endpoint is missing here, it is missing from the server too.

arriving while the search runs joins it instead of starting another. The

one and a cache hit never runs a search.

The simulation is pure CPU on an unauthenticated route, so the body is
bounds-checked first and the work then runs on the blocking pool under
admission control.
post.description:
Memoised: the result is a pure function of the body and the loaded game
data (no clock, no RNG, no user scoping), so two people posting the same
configuration get the same three floats. The UI compares configurations by
firing a burst of these at once, which was filling the admission queue; a
burst of repeats costs one simulation.

Validation stays AHEAD of the cache read so an out-of-range body is rejected
rather than keyed, and the cache read sits ahead of `cpu::run` so a hit never
consumes a permit.

200.description: Skill-window DPS, total damage over the window, and the cycle average.

503.description: The CPU admission queue is full. Retry shortly.

AccountFactsReq.description:
Player-declared account state the sync cannot read (the "account facts"
prompt). With no declaration the never-guess default stands: the dependent
skills price 0.

open_recruit_slots.description:
Recruit slots purchased beyond the initial one (0-3). Prices the
per-slot HR-speed riders (Lin's Meritocracy).

training_class.description:
The class currently training in the Training Room ("Guard", "Sniper",
...). Lets trainer hints rank class-specific skills honestly instead
of recommending a Guard trainer for a Sniper.

entity_id.description: Id in the kind's own space, e.g. `char_002_amiya` for an operator.

ArchiveClip.description: One recorded line, in every language whose file is on disk.

ArchiveFile.description: One of the archive's files or diaries: a page of prose with its own plate.

date.description: The in-setting date the file is stamped with (`1097.10.27`).

titlePictureUrl.description: The drawn title over the page, on 4 of the 16 EN files.

engName.description:
The landmark's name in the setting's own Latin spelling, dropped when
it repeats `name` (15 of the 26 EN landmarks repeat it).

ArchiveLogChapter.description:
A run of log entries under one of the archive's own chapter headers, in
the order the chapter lists them.

chapterIcon.description:
`NORMAL` or `SPECIAL`, the header's own glyph. Kept raw: no art is
joined to it, because the two values are the whole vocabulary.

displayId.description:
The number the chapter header prints (`01`), a string because the
table writes it padded.

logoUrl.description: The small masthead glyph, and the big one the story is headed with.

oneOf.description: The masthead this story ran under.

lines.description: The body, already split by the table into prose and pictures.

name.description:
The picture's name, kept so a line with no file on disk still says
what is missing.

ArchiveNewsLine.description: One line of a news body: prose, or a picture that runs in the column.

pictureType.description:
`IMAGE`, `ENDING_IMAGE` or `ROGUE_IMAGE`, raw from the table. All 57
pictures on the EN library groups are `IMAGE`; the other two values
belong to the `rogue_*` archives the library does not list.

url.description:
The AVG image, resolved through the same tree a script's `[Image]`
name resolves through.

ArchiveRecordingNode.description:
One node of the recordings shelf: a titled set of clips the player unlocks
together.

bench.description:
True for a SPARE-seat pick (Control-Center bench top-up after every
value-seated operator): parked for lowest opportunity cost, not for its
skills. The frontend badges these so a gated skill text on a
benchwarmer doesn't read as the optimizer's reasoning.

parked.description:
True for a PARKED token: seated at zero morale on purpose so a named
plant-count gate and a robot-exclusion gate both apply (the "dead
Lancet"). Never rotated; its own skills are not live.

yield_lmd_per_day.description:
Realized daily output (the gold->trade loop is coupled: LMD = min(gold
made, gold sold) × 500). This is the value the optimizer maximizes - the
per-room efficiency %s are just for display.

yield_total_value.description: LMD-equivalent of everything combined (LMD + EXP at 1:1).

BodySize.description:
The body TEXTURE's size in pixels, which is the unit `facePos` is measured
in. 1024 for most bodies, 1280 for the oversized ones, and a face patch's
fraction of the plate is `facePos / bodySize` in both cases. Absent only
when neither the hub nor the PNG header could be read.

BuildChoice.description:
One option in a community default distribution, with the count that put it
there. Ordered most-picked first by the query.

id.description:
`skillId` for a skill, `uniEquipId` for a module. Always a stable id:
`skillIndex` is resolved here, against the same game data that produced
the operator's `skills` array, so no client indexes by position.

skillIndex.description:
The game's 0-based skill index. Present for skills only, and carried for
display ("S3") rather than for lookup.

skillLevel.description: Explicit pre-mastery skill level (1-7). Overrides `mastery_level` when set.

CatalogResponse.description:
The facility catalogue, straight out of `building_data`. The client renders
capacities, power draw and level caps from this instead of carrying its own
copy of numbers the game already publishes.

shift_count.description:
Shifts in a base day. A game constant, not a property of any one
player - a base whose rooms only queue two presets still runs three
shifts, alternating across them.

slots.description: The floorplan every base shares - what the client draws the board from.

CatalogSlotDto.description:
One slot of the base floorplan, joined to a player's rooms on `slot_id`.

Coordinates stay in the game's own half-tile units rather than pixels or
grid tracks: how a half-tile becomes a column is the board's decision, and
the elevator shafts (1 unit wide where every room is 2) only make sense at
this scale.

category.description: Room category this slot accepts, matching `CatalogRoomDto::category`.

offset_row.description:
Absolute - the storey's Y-offset is already applied. Counts up from the
bottom of the base, so B4 is 0.

unlock_control_level.description: Control-centre level that unlocks this floor.

ChapterRange.description: An inclusive run of mainline chapter numbers, `from <= to`.

oneOf.description:
The `body_url` texture's own size. `face_pos` divided by THIS is the
patch's fraction of the body plate.

The canvas rect the whole plate is drawn into, from the character's own
prefab root. It is the bundle's, so every sprite of a folder shares it.

intervals.description: Steady-state losses at each check-in cadence.

next_full_hours.description:
Hours (from an empty buffer, i.e. from a claim now) until the FIRST
production room's buffer is full - log in before this to lose nothing.

firstPullAt.description: Unix seconds. None when the corpus is empty.

averageEncountered.description: Mean number of distinct enemies encountered across every synced user.

handbookTotal.description: Visible handbook size, matching the per-user response's denominator.

userCount.description: Number of users in the average's denominator (those with synced enemy data).

DeletePlansResponse.description: Result of a bulk plan delete.

deleted.description: Plans removed. Ids the caller had no plan for are not counted.

removed.description:
Whether there were stored credentials to remove. Disconnecting twice is
not an error; the second call reports `false`.

comfort_upside_per_hour.description:
Recovery/hr still on the table if ambience were maxed:
`(limit - comfort) / 2500`.

occupant_aura_per_hour.description:
The strongest whole-dorm recovery aura among the DRAFTED occupants
("+X/hr to all Operators in that Dormitory", non-stacking).

occupant_single_per_hour.description:
The strongest single-target heal among the drafted occupants
("+X/hr to another Operator whose Morale is not full").

recovery_per_hour.description: Game-true rate for THIS dorm (`DormData.Phases[level]`), before skills.

DormsDto.description:
The dormitories' contribution. They produce nothing, so they never appear in
a `BaseAssignment` - but they set how fast workers recover and how many can
rest at once, which is what decides whether a staffing survives its own
rhythm. Surfaced separately so "no yield" doesn't read as "not accounted for".

per_dorm.description:
Each dormitory, BEST FIRST - the order resters fill them. A 2/5/2's
under-leveled dorms show up here as the slower rates they are.

recovery_per_hour.description: Morale restored per hour to a resting operator, scaled by dorm levels.

total_capacity.description: Operators the base can rest at once.

total_levels.description: Sum of dorm levels - the `&dorm&lv` scaling the clause engine reads.

DraftRoom.description:
One room of a client-drafted layout. Mirrors `UserRoom` minus the bits only
the live game data can supply (preset queues).

comfort.description:
Dormitory ambience (0-5000), carried through from the synced base so a
drafted dorm keeps its furniture bonus. 0 elsewhere.

formula_type.description: Factory recipe ("`F_GOLD`" / "`F_EXP`" / "`F_DIAMOND`"). None for other rooms.

operators.description: Who the player has placed here in the draft.

DraftRoomDto.description:
The serialized twin of [`DraftRoom`] - what the client sends back on every
evaluate/optimize call.

DronesDto.description: The drone (Labor) buffer, projected to now from the synced snapshot.

full_in_hours.description: Hours until the buffer caps and recovery is wasted. `None` = already full.

encounteredCount.description: Number of distinct enemies the user has encountered.

enemies.description: Encountered enemies, enriched and sorted by handbook `sortId`.

handbookTotal.description:
Number of enemies visible in the handbook (excludes `hideInHandbook`),
i.e. the denominator for a completion ratio.

name.description:
Handbook display fields; `None` when the encountered id isn't present in
the loaded `enemy_handbook_table` (e.g. an unreleased/unknown variant).

EntityKind.description:
What a tier list placement ranks. The id space of each kind is its own, so a
placement is keyed by (kind, id), and the variants are the allow-list: an
unknown kind fails to parse at the route and never reaches the database.

EntityKinds.description: A list's offered kinds, as stored in `tier_lists.entity_kinds`.

EntitySummary.description: The display form of one entity: enough for a tile, a pool filter and a link.

facets.description:
Kind-specific tags the tile and the pool filters read. Operators carry
`rarity`, `profession`, `sub_profession_id`, `position`, and, when set,
`nation_id`, `appellation`, and the server's own `profession_name`,
`sub_profession_name` and `nation_name`. Subclasses carry
`profession` and the server's `profession_name`; enemies
`enemy_level` and `enemy_index`; events `display_type`, `type`,
`start_time` (unix seconds) and, for a rerun, `rerun`; factions
`power_level` (`nation`, `group` or `team`); Stronghold bonds
`bond_type` (`season` or `regular`) and, for a season bond, `power_ids`.
Skins carry `char_id`, `operator` (the wearer's name), `rarity`,
`profession` and, when filed under one, `brand`; modules `char_id`,
`operator`, `profession`, `module_type` (`X`, `Y`, `D`, `A`, `B`) and
`type_code` (`SUM`); skills `char_id`, `operator`, `profession`, `slot`
(`1` to `3`) and, when the skill has levels, `skill_type` and
`sp_type`; Integrated Strategies entries `theme` (`rogue_N`,
which is IS N+1) and `item_type` (`theme`, `relic`, `band`, ...);
story sprites `source` (`operator` or `npc`), for an operator `char_id`,
and, when the hub places the face, `face` (`x,y` fractions of the plate);
main story episodes `episode` (`0` to `16` on EN), `act` (the
`chapter_table` index) and `act_name`.

href.description: Site route for the entity's own page, when it has one.

icon.description:
Image path under the API root (`/avatar/char_002_amiya`), server-neutral:
the client prefixes its own base and server. `None` when the extract
holds no art for the entity.

ErrorBody.description:
The single error envelope every failing endpoint returns.

Public because it is the documented error schema: `openapi.rs` registers it
as a component and handlers reference it from their `responses(...)` lists.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable code. Clients should branch on this, not on
`message`, which is prose and may change.

claim_interval_hours.description: Extra check-in cadence (hours) to price alongside the 6/12/24 presets.

ignore_promotion.description:
Plan with every operator's highest base skills, whether or not the
player has promoted them that far. The result is a target to build
toward, not a reading of the base they have today.

oneOf.description:
Check-in economics: time until the first room stalls, and what each
claim cadence loses. `None` when nothing produces.

dorms.description: What the dormitory wing is worth to this layout.

oneOf.description: Drone buffer, projected to now. `None` when the sync carries none.

morale_synced_hours_ago.description:
Hours since the newest morale write in the sync - how stale the
"current bar" data is. `None` when the sync carries no morale.

power.description: Facility power: generated, consumed, and the net the base runs at.

sustain.description: How long each stationed operator lasts before morale runs out.

trainer_hints.description:
Top trainers for the declared `training_class` fact (empty otherwise,
or when the layout has no Training Room).

oneOf.description:
The drafted crews simulated with NO rotation at all - "if you never
swap". `None` when nothing is staffed. Seeded with PROJECTED live
morale, so its clock starts now, not at a hypothetical full bar.

EventShop.description:
An event's token shop as the planner shows it: the game server's goods
(see `gamedata::types::event_shop`) with the names and icons the client
tables give them.

maxPrice.description: Token cost of every limited good at full stock, the server's figure.

server.description:
Which server's shop this is: CN when that account has fetched it,
else EN.

FacePos.description:
Where a face patch sits on its body, in BODY PIXELS: `x`,`y` are the
patch's top-left corner measured from the body's left and TOP edge, `w`,`h`
the on-body size the face texture is scaled into. Haak reads
`{x: 512, y: 120, w: 51, h: 71}` from the hub's `facePos (512,120,0)` /
`faceSize (51,71)`. Absent on a legacy hub's `(-1,-1)`/`(0,0)` sentinel, on
a whole-body sprite, and on any folder whose `hub.json` the unpacker has
not written yet.

FacetValue.description:
One facet value: a single tag, or several (an enemy's several levels, an
event's several factions).

idle_hours.description:
Hours of lost work: shifts the room rested dark plus the remainder of
blocks after its crew ran dry.

lmd.description: Simulated totals over the horizon, in the room's own resources.

FavoriteState.description: Whether the caller has this tier list favourited.

FieldError.description: One field-level failure inside a `VALIDATION_FAILED` response.

field.description: The offending field, as named in the request body.

message.example: must be a valid email address

GalleryGroup.description:
One archive's pictures: an event (`act13side`) or an Integrated
Strategies theme (`rogue_1`), by its archive component id.

name.description: The event's or theme's name, or the id when the data names neither.

pictures.description: In the order the archive shows them.

GalleryPicture.description:
One gallery picture. Its 320 px and 1600 px JPEGs are
`/story/gallery/{id}/thumb` and `/story/gallery/{id}/header`.

id.description: The table's key, `act13side_pic_0`: what a profile background stores.

url.description: The original PNG, absent when the file is not on disk.

GameDataHealth.description:
Tables that fell back to an empty default on the most recent load, per server.

Deliberately does NOT flip the top-level `status`: a degraded table is a data
problem, not an availability one, and paging an uptime monitor for a cosmetic
table would train everyone to ignore it. Report it, don't alarm on it.

GamedataOverride.description:
`gamedata_overrides` row - a hand-entered replacement for one field of one
game-data entity in one locale.

can_edit.description: The caller may save or delete it: its owner, or a site admin.

cells.description: Row-major: cell `(r, c)` is `cells[r * cols + c]`.

entity_kinds.description: The kinds a cell may hold, in canonical order.

kinds_locked.description:
`entity_kinds` is set by the template this grid was forked from and a
save cannot change it. True for every fork, including one whose
`template_of` is hidden from this viewer; false once the source is
deleted, which clears the link.

oneOf.description: `None` for an original, or when the source has been deleted.

`None` when the cell is empty, or when no loaded server's game data has
such an entity; the raw `entity_kind` and `entity_id` are still sent.

entity_server.description:
The server `entity` was resolved on when the reader's server does not
know it (an operator only CN has released), so its icon is fetched
from that server. `None` when it resolved on the reader's server, or
did not resolve.

GridCellInput.description:
One cell as the editor sends it. `entity_kind` and `entity_id` are set
together or not at all.

GridInput.description:
A whole grid as the editor saves it. `cells` is row-major and exactly
`rows * cols` long, and every pick is of a kind in `entity_kinds`.

entity_kinds.description:
The kinds a cell may hold: at least one. Stored deduplicated and in
canonical order. A fork's set is its template's and cannot change.

name.description: The owner's in-game nickname, or their uid when it is empty.

GridPreviewIcon.description:
One filled cell of a card thumbnail: its art's path, the kind (which
decides how the art sits in the cell), and the server to fetch it from
when it is not the reader's, with [`GridCell::entity_server`]'s meaning.

entity_kinds.description: The kinds a cell may hold, in canonical order.

preview.description:
The board in miniature for a card thumbnail: one entry per cell,
row-major like [`Grid::cells`], `rows * cols` long. `None` for an
empty cell, and for a pick no loaded server knows or that has no art.

GridTemplateRef.description: The grid a fork was made from.

base_hps.description: Heal-per-second during the SP-charge phase (0 for burst healers).

skill_hps.description: Heal-per-second while the active skill is up.

IllustrationItem.description:
One background or CG a group's stories reference, with the stories that
reference it. `url` is `null` when the name resolves to no file on disk:
the tab lists the name and says so rather than dropping it.

ImageSize.description:
A background or CG plate's own metrics: `w`,`h` the sprite rect in texture
px and `ppu` its pixels-per-unit. A command with no `screenadapt` draws it
`w * 100 / ppu` by `h * 100 / ppu` canvas px, 100 being the reference
pixels-per-unit every AVG `CanvasScaler` carries. `ppu_assumed` says the
100 is a FALLBACK, not a read: the size came from the PNG header because no
`sprites.json` covered that name.

ItemCatalog.description:
The item picker's data: every held item, and the population the holder
counts are cut from, so a row can say what share of players hold it.

population.description:
Visible players under the same gate and server filter as `holders`,
so `holders / population` is a share of the same people.

ItemHoldingSummary.description:
How many visible players hold an item, the largest single holding, and
how much of it they hold between them. Drives the item picker so it
never offers an item nobody holds.

total_quantity.description:
Every visible holding of the item summed: how much of it exists
across the ranked population.

ItemLeaderboardEntry.description:
One row of the inventory leaderboard: a player and how much of the
requested item they hold. Identity fields mirror `LeaderboardEntry` so the
same row components render both.

grade.description:
The player's score grade, so a row reads the same whichever metric
ranks it.

rank.description: `rank()` over quantity among visible holders: ties share a rank.

total.description: Visible holders of the item: the population the page is cut from.

total_quantity.description:
Every holding in that population summed: how much of the item exists
across the ranked players.

ItemStanding.description: One player's place on the leaderboard for one item.

rank_global.description: Rank among every visible holder, and that population's size.

rank_server.description:
Rank among visible holders on the player's own server, and that
population's size.

LayoutResponse.description:
The player's real base, every built slot of it.

This exists because a `BaseAssignment` is deliberately NOT a layout: it
carries only the rooms the plan has something to say about (production, plus
a staffed Control Center). Seeding a planner from it silently drops
dormitories, power plants and every support facility - which then breaks the
power balance AND the scoring, since dorm levels and facility counts feed
the clause engine.

facts.description: The owner's saved account facts, so every viewer scores with them.

presets.description:
The player's own saved shift rotation, straight out of `presetQueue`.
Separate from `rooms` because that is the round-trip shape the client
posts back; presets are read-only context and never travel with a draft.

rank_delta.description:
Rank change vs. the snapshot baseline for the requested movement interval.
Positive = climbed. `None` when the caller didn't request movement data
or no baseline snapshot exists for the user yet.

LevelBucket.description: One bucket of an investment histogram.

level.description:
Mastery 0..3 for a skill, or module level 0..3 where 0 means the owner
has not unlocked it. 0 is a real answer in both cases, and the largest
bucket in most: it is where people stop, not missing data.

LevelTarget.description: Where the walk stops for each operator.

LineDisposition.description:
How a zero-marginal line should be read.

Serialized straight into `SkillLineDto`, so the generated TS binding is a
union rather than a bare `string`: the frontend switches on these values.

LmdIncomeDto.description:
LMD the account earns in a day, and the days until `lmd_missing` is
covered - once from the base and mission chests alone, once with every
day's natural sanity spent on the LMD farming stage.

base_per_day.description:
The synced base's realized LMD per day as stationed right now (the
Score tab's current figure). `None` without a synced base.

dailies_per_day.description:
The live daily mission chests (weekday and weekend groups weighted by
their days) plus the live weekly chests over seven days, LMD only,
every chest claimed.

days_with_farming.description: The same with the farming stage's LMD added.

days_without_farming.description:
Days until the shortfall is earned from the base and dailies: 0 when
nothing is missing, `None` when nothing is earned.

farming_runs_per_day.description: Runs of that stage a day's natural sanity regeneration buys.

farming_stage.description: The stage the farming estimate runs (the LMD stage, CE-6).

Locale.description:
`locales` table. `gamedata_server` names the Arknights client whose text
serves this locale's operator/skill/stage strings.

is_source.description:
The locale the source text is written in. Complete by definition: its
text is `ui_message_keys.source_text`, not a `ui_messages` row.

exp_owned.description: EXP held as cards (every EXP item times its EXP value).

income.description: What the account earns in a day and how long the LMD shortfall takes.

lmd_owned.description: The synced LMD balance; 0 when the profile carries none.

operators.description: Every remaining operator, most expensive first.

operators_remaining.description: Owned operators not yet at their target.

operators_total.description: Owned operators the game data knows.

MaxLevelOperatorDto.description: One operator still short of its target, with what closing the gap costs.

exp.description: EXP for the remaining levels, across every promotion on the way.

ModuleLevelStats.description: How far E2 owners take one module's level.

end.description: The final sample - the bar they end the week on.

room_type.description:
The room they call home in the rotation (most-worked slot; a permanent
dorm resident's dormitory).

MusicCue.description: A music cue: the intro plays once, the loop repeats.

value.description:
Effect % in that facility's own units (clue collection speed,
Specialization training speed, HR contacting speed).

OpStage.description: One stage that awards Originite Prime on first clear.

enum: Unknown as requested by management agency

OperatorBuildStatsResponse.description:
What the community defaults to for one operator: which skill they leave
selected, and which module they leave equipped.

The distributions are whole, not just the winner, because 12 of 364
operators have a modal share under 50% and there the runner-up is as
informative as the leader. `skillTotal` and `moduleTotal` are the
denominators, and they differ: skills count E2 owners, modules count only
owners with an ADVANCED module actually equipped, which is 13.63% of rows.

masteries.description:
Mastery histogram per skill, and level histogram per module: where
people STOP investing rather than what they picked. Empty below the
reporting floor, like the distributions above.

minSample.description:
Below this many samples a distribution is withheld entirely, so a rare
operator's numbers cannot describe a handful of identifiable accounts.

OperatorIndexEntry.description:
Compact operator record for client-side search palettes and autocompletes.
Order of fields matches the JSON contract - keep stable.

dateOfBirth.description:
The profile's `dateOfBirth` verbatim (e.g. "October 4"), empty when the
operator has no profile. A plain string rather than an `Option` so a
cached index from before this field fails to deserialize and is rebuilt.

gender.description:
From the operator profile - list page gender/race/birthplace filters and
the randomizer "Feline" challenge (`race`). Defaulted when no profile.

groupId.description: Faction group id (list page "factions" filter + faction-logo fallback).

hasOffensiveRecovery.description:
Randomizer challenge-filter booleans, precomputed so the randomizer
doesn't need the full `/static/operators` table. `hasOffensiveRecovery` /
`hasDefensiveRecovery`: any skill level with the matching `spType`.
`allSkillsManual`: has >=1 skill and every skill's first level is manual.

oneOf.description: `itemObtainApproach` as a category, the same on every server.

phaseMaxLevels.description:
`maxLevel` per elite phase; its length is the phase count. With
`skillCount`, `potentialRankCount` and `modules`, this is what the
profile Stats tab reads instead of the `/static/operators` table.

portrait.description: Small portrait image path (grid card image src).

professionName.description:
The server's own names for `profession`, `subProfessionId`,
`nationId`, `groupId` and `teamId`, so a client need not keep an
English table per id. `None` when the server's table does not name the
id.

rarity.description: 1-6. Converts from the game's `TIER_N` enum so the frontend doesn't have to.

stats.description:
Max-level, max-elite base stats, flattened so the list page can sort
without pulling `phases`/`attributesKeyFrames`.

teamId.description: Sub-faction / team id (same faction filter + logo fallback).

voiceActors.description:
Every `cvName` across the operator's voice languages, deduplicated, so
the list page's voice-actor filter doesn't need the `/static/voices` table.

OperatorIndexModule.description:
The module fields the profile Stats tab reads: id to match the roster, type
to pick the advanced ones, type names for the gap-list label.

OperatorIndexStats.description: Flattened final-phase base stats for the operators list sorters.

OperatorOwnershipCounts.description:
One operator's community counts. Struct-valued rather than a bare owner
tally so the next statistic is a field here instead of a fourth map
travelling alongside in the response.

e2Owners.description:
Owners who took this operator to E2.

Zero is NOT a community signal for the 36 operators that cannot reach
E2 at all: one to three stars carry fewer than three phases, so their
rate is structurally zero. Clients must suppress the figure for those
rather than rank them last.

OperatorOwnershipResponse.description:
Population-level ownership: how many sharing players own each operator, plus
the denominator. Only operators with at least one owner are listed; a missing
id implies zero owners. `totalUsers` is the eligible population on this
server (players who imported a roster and opted into stat sharing).

met.description:
The plan has nothing left to do: the operator is owned and every
target (promotion and level, skill level, each mastery, each module
stage) is reached or passed. Read from the same roster state the
material diff uses, so a met plan contributes no materials.

enum: Unknown as requested by management agency

avatarUrl.description:
The `ui_char_avatar_*` sprite as an asset-index path
(`/textures/spritepack/...`), the same form the operators list's
`portrait` and a group's `coverUrl` carry: the frontend serves it
under `/api/assets`. Empty when no avatar resolves (0 of 315 on EN).

illustrationCount.description: Distinct backgrounds plus distinct CGs over this operator's records.

name.description: The operator's name from the character table.

profession.description:
The character table's profession, the raw game value the operators
list carries (`PIONEER`, `WARRIOR`, ...).

professionName.description:
The server's own name for `profession`, from its gacha class tags.
`None` when the character table has no such operator.

rarity.description:
1-6 stars, the same `u8` the operators list's `rarity` carries; 0 when
the character table has no such operator (0 of 315 on EN).

spriteCount.description: Distinct sprite folders over this operator's records.

wordCount.description: The sum of this operator's records' `wordCount`.

excluded.description: Operators the plan may not seat anywhere (injured, saved for elsewhere).

ignore_promotion.description:
Plan with every operator's highest base skills, whether or not the
player has promoted them that far. The result is a target to build
toward, not a reading of the base they have today.

locked.description: Operators the plan must keep exactly where the draft puts them.

scope.description:
Slot ids the optimizer may restaff. Empty = every room in the layout.
Rooms outside the scope keep their drafted crews AND hold those
operators, so a scoped run can't quietly steal from an untouched room.

oneOf.description:
`None` when the served game data has no such entity (a CN-only operator
read on EN, an id from a removed kind). The placement is still served,
so the client can show it rather than silently drop it.

PlacementDetail.description: A stored placement and what it points at in the served game data.

pinned.description: Pinned groups list first. See `list_groups` for the order.

craftBlocked.description:
True when the item has a workshop recipe the player cannot use yet
because its room or stage gates are unmet. False when it is craftable
or has no usable recipe at all.

oneOf.description:
The crafting recipe, when this item has one.

This closes a genuine cycle in the data: a recipe's costs are themselves
`PlanRequirementItem`s, which may in turn be craftable. ts-rs emits
mutually referencing types and handles it, but utoipa inlines nested
schemas while collecting them and would recurse until the stack runs
out, so the cycle is cut here and the schema emits a `$ref` instead.
Removing this attribute makes the whole `OpenAPI` document unbuildable,
which takes the server down at startup rather than failing a test.

unmetStages.description:
Stage clears the item's workshop recipe waits on that the player has
not made, in recipe order. The same gates `craft_reason` names as
`Stage <code>`, structured so a client can link each stage. Empty when
the item has no recipe or its stage gates are all met.

PlanUnmetStage.description: One stage clear a recipe is still waiting on.

code.description: Display code (`S9-3`), or the stage id when the stage table lacks it.

lastSyncedAt.description:
When the caller's account was last synced to our database. Every
current-state reading behind the plan (roster, inventory, base, stage
clears) is a snapshot as of this moment. Null for an account with no
profile row.

operatorRequirements.description:
Each counted plan's own requirements, by operator id. Present only when
the request asked for `by_operator`.

PlateRect.description:
The plate a character is drawn into, in CANVAS px: the prefab root rect the
bundle ships, `x`,`y` its anchored position over the slot origin and
`w`,`h` its size. Amiya legacy reads `{x: 0, y: 203, w: 1090, h: 1090}`,
Haak `{x: 0, y: 150, w: 955, h: 955}`. It WINS over the slot template's
1024 at y 203, so two characters in one frame are drawn at different sizes.
Absent when the folder has no `hub.json`, or one written before the
unpacker read the root rect.

name.description:
1 to 100 characters after trimming. Saving under an existing name
replaces that preset's target.

PresetTarget.description:
A preset's target, independent of rarity: a bulk-add applies it to each
selected operator and clamps it to what that operator can reach.

display_on_profile.description:
Whether plans made from it show on the public profile. Absent in
presets saved before this field existed, which read as private.

level.description: Level at that promotion. Null means the operator's cap at `elite`.

masteries.description: Mastery per skill index, each 0 to 3.

ProfileBackground.description:
`profile_layout.background`: a reference to game art, never a URL. The
client builds the URL from the kind and id with the helpers every other
page uses.

elite.description:
Which elite art an operator background draws: `1` or `2`. `None` is the
art the header drew before the choice existed, elite 2 where the
operator has it, else elite 1. Kept on the operator kind alone, so an
outfit or a gallery picture never carries it.

focus_x.description:
Where the crop centres, as a percentage of the art's width, 0 to 100.
`None` is the centre.

scale.description:
How far the art is zoomed in past `cover`, as a percentage,
[`BACKGROUND_SCALE_MIN`] to [`BACKGROUND_SCALE_MAX`]. `None` is 100,
the art exactly covering the header as it did before zoom existed.

ProfileBackgroundKind.description:
What art a profile header may show. `skin` and `operator` are tier-list
entity kinds, so their ids are checked by the same lookup a favourites
block is, and their art is a painted figure the game ships a 1024 px
reduced copy of beside the full one (469 of 474 outfit arts, 323 of 381
elite 2 arts on EN 2026-10-05). `archive_pic` is a landscape picture,
checked against `story_review_meta_table` instead.

Ruled out by measurement on EN 2026-10-05, none of them wide enough or
small enough for a header about 1100 px wide: event art (`/event-image`)
is 280x166; a main story key visual is a 432 px square poster with the
chapter title typeset into it; an Archives entry picture is 420x508
portrait. An Archives gallery picture is 1600x900 and right for the
header but 2.05 MB on average (324 pictures), and only 48 of the 324 have
the game's 260x148 gallery thumbnail, so `archive_pic` is served through
`/story/gallery/{id}/{thumb,header}`, 320 px and 1600 px JPEGs.

`story_cg` and `story_scene` are the story scripts' own art (1,230 CGs
and 898 scene plates on EN 2026-10-06 pass the header filter of at
least 1024 px, 1.6 to 1.9 wide over high and 0.2 PNG bytes per px),
checked against `/story/art-gallery/{kind}` and served through it the
same way.

ProfileLayout.description:
How the owner arranged their profile, `user_settings.profile_layout`.

Stored as a jsonb object of three keys: `tabs` (the order and visibility
of every tab), `showcase` (the Showcase tab's blocks) and `background` (the
header art); a save sets only the keys it sends. Deserializing goes
through [`ProfileLayout::normalize`], so every value that reaches the
code, from the database, the cache or a request body, holds each known tab
exactly once.

What a visitor receives is [`ProfileLayout::visible_only`]: a private tab is
absent from it, not present with `visible: false`.

oneOf.description:
The art behind the profile header. `None` when the stored layout has
none, which renders the header exactly as before backgrounds existed.
Not gated by any tab: the header is the profile itself.

The Showcase tab's blocks. `None` when the stored layout has no
`showcase` key: a save that leaves the key out keeps the stored
showcase (see `queries::users::update_settings`), so a client that only
knows about tabs cannot wipe it.

ProfileLayoutPatch.description:
A save of `profile_layout`: only the keys the request carried, each
normalized as [`ProfileLayout::normalize`] reads it. A key left out keeps
the stored value, so the tab editor sends only `tabs`, the showcase editor
only `showcase` and the background picker only `background`, and none can
wipe another's work (see `queries::users::update_settings`). The one save
that clears the whole layout is the tab editor's explicit Reset, which
sends `null` instead of a patch.

`tabs` is present when the request carried a `tabs` array, `showcase` when
it carried a `showcase` object. `background` is present whenever the key
is: `null`, or a value that does not normalize, clears it.

ProfileShowcase.description: `profile_layout.showcase`: the owner's blocks, in display order.

visible.description:
False hides the tab from visitors and refuses its data to them. The
owner always sees and reads every tab.

ProfileTabId.description:
One tab of the player profile page. The variants are the allow-list and
their declaration order is the canonical order, the one the profile showed
before layouts existed: a layout that omits a tab gets it back in this
position's turn, visible.

own_gap_days.description:
The group's own last EN listing gap in days when it dated the
rerun; `None` when the pooled median did.

oneOf.description:
A CN outfit-shop listing EN has shipped past without carrying: EN's
recommend panel has no entry with its tag, and holds a later tag
whose CN entry started at or after it. Never dated.

poolCutoff.description:
Newest CN release date this edition stocks; the pool is every
`ReviewOutfit` with `cn_get_time` at or before it.

capacity.description:
Output-buffer size: orders for a trading post (incl. crew capacity
skills), items for a factory. Evaluate path only.

fill_hours.description:
Hours from an empty buffer to full - how long the room runs unattended
before it stalls. Evaluate path only.

ledger.description: Per-skill contribution breakdown (evaluate path only; empty elsewhere).

locked.description:
True when this is a FIXED synergy squad (operators depend on each other and
can't be swapped); false = flexible / interchangeable team.

non_production.description:
Non-production effects this crew provides (Control Center only): clue /
training / HR speed in each boosted facility's OWN units - never folded
into the LMD objective. Empty for other rooms.

order_value.description:
Order-VALUE % (LMD per order, e.g. Proviso) - multiplies LMD yield without
inflating the speed %.

total_efficiency.description: Order-acquisition SPEED % (the productivity bonus the game shows).

yield_lmd_per_day.description: Per-room natural yield (trading posts show potential LMD if gold-supplied).

RotationRequest.description:
A rotation is whole-base by construction (a shift covers every room at
once), so unlike optimize there is no `scope` - only who must stay put.

ignore_promotion.description:
Plan with every operator's highest base skills, whether or not the
player has promoted them that far. The result is a target to build
toward, not a reading of the base they have today.

ScoreHistoryPoint.description: One point of a user's leaderboard history - a snapshot they appeared in.

SearchEntry.description:
One player search row: the profile plus the value of the sort that
ranked it. `metric` is the count for a count sort and `register_ts` for
the join-date sort; it is `None` under the score sort, where the
profile's `total_score` already is the value.

availCount.description: Purchase limit; `-1` is unlimited stock, which the buy-out leaves out.

ShopGoodKind.description:
What a shop good is, for grouping; the server's `item_type` is kept beside
it for anything finer.

ShopItem.description:
An item as the shop names it: the client table's name and icon, EN when
the item exists there.

oneOf.description: A row of favourite entities of one kind, any kind a tier list can rank.

ids.description: Display order, at most [`SHOWCASE_MAX_IDS`], no repeats.

title.description:
Plain text, trimmed, at most [`SHOWCASE_TITLE_MAX`] characters.
`None` shows the kind's own name.

oneOf.description: A grid, by slug. Unlisted grids count: they are served by slug.
A tier list, by slug. Unlisted lists count too.

One of the owner's plans shown on their profile. A visitor gets it only
while the Plans tab is visible to them.

operator_id.description:
The plan's operator. Deleting a plan and planning the operator
again makes a new row with a new id; the block follows the
operator to it instead of reading as removed. Absent on blocks
saved before 2026-10-07, which still match by `id` alone.

ShowcaseBlock.description:
One showcase block. Every block points at something that already exists on
the site; the only text an owner types is a favourites block's title.

ShowcaseBlockView.description: One block, with what it points at checked and, for favourites, resolved.

entities.description:
Favourites only, one per id in `block`, in its order; empty for every
other block. A visitor is sent only the ids that resolve.

removed.description:
What the block points at is gone: a deleted grid or tier list, a plan
deleted or no longer shown on the profile, or favourites none of whose
ids the game data knows. Only the owner is ever sent such a block.

ShowcaseEntity.description:
One favourite, resolved against the reader's server first and then every
other loaded server, as a grid cell is.

oneOf.description: `None` when no loaded server's game data has the id.

entity_server.description:
The server `entity` resolved on when the reader's does not know it,
with `GridCell::entity_server`'s meaning.

SkillLineDto.description:
One line of a room's per-skill breakdown (the deep dive's "how this is
calculated"). Values are MARGINALS in this exact crew - what the room's
number loses if this one skill is removed - so pair riders, non-stacking
rules and faction gates are already folded in.

disposition.description: How to read a zero-marginal line.

from_control_center.description: The line's owner sits in the Control Center, not this room.

note.description: A reading aid for marginals spread over other lines (count skills).

operator_name.description:
Display name, so Control-Center lines shown on another room need no
roster join client-side.

SkillMasteryStats.description: How far E2 owners take one skill's mastery.

buckets.description:
Ascending by level, always covering 0..3 with zero-filled gaps so a
client can render a fixed strip without reasoning about absence.

skillId.description:
Stable id, resolved from the stored index against the same game data
that produces the operator's `skills` array.

counts.description:
Map of `skin_id` -> number of owners. Only non-default skins (`skin_id`
containing `@`) are included; absent IDs imply zero owners.

totalUsers.description:
Number of users counted in the denominator - every user that has any
skin record (i.e. has imported their data at least once).

SlotPresetsDto.description: One slot's saved rotation: the crew the player has queued for each shift.

SpriteItem.description:
One character sprite folder a group's stories reference. `bodyUrl` is the
`$1` body, the same file `GET /story/{id}` resolves a bare name to, and
`faces` counts the DISTINCT `#N` variants the group's scripts ask for.

StatusOk.description:
The `{"status":"ok"}` success body for endpoints that return no payload.

The type IS the documented schema and the serialized body, so there is no
second declaration to keep in agreement. It reached the wire as an untyped
`serde_json::json!` before, which meant the `OpenAPI` document described it
from a hand-written copy.

StoryArchive.description:
Everything the game's own "from the archive" screen shows for one group.

An archive is a group's, not a story's: it belongs to the event and is
unlocked by playing it. A group with no archive answers 200 with an empty
`sections`, because "this event kept no archive" is an answer and a 404 is
not.

hidden.description:
The clips the shelf hides until they are unlocked, which belong to
no node (8 of `main_14`'s 43).

StoryArchiveSection.description:
One item of a group's archive: a log entry, a landmark, a news story, a
file, a gallery picture, a track or a recording.

The sections are a TAGGED list rather than a fixed record because an
archive carries two or three of them and never all seven: on EN
`act13side` is news, files and a gallery, `act17side` is logs, landmarks
and a gallery, `act25side` is files and a gallery, `main_14` is nothing
but recordings. `count` is the LEAF count, the number of rows the game's
own screen lists, so `logs` counts logs and not the chapters they are
grouped into, and `recordings` counts clips and not nodes.

StoryArtGallery.description:
`GET /story/art-gallery/{kind}`: every story CG or scene wide enough for
a profile header, each once, under the first library group whose
scripts draw it.

StoryArtGroup.description: One library group's newly seen pictures.

StoryArtKind.description:
Which story-script art a [`StoryArtGallery`] lists: `cg`, an `Image`
still from `textures/avg/imgs`, or `scene`, a `Background` plate from
`textures/avg/bg`. Decided by the tree the file resolves into, not by the
command that names it, so an `Image` that falls back to a `bg/` file is a
scene.

StoryArtPicture.description:
One CG or scene. Its 320 px and up-to-1600 px JPEGs are
`/story/art-gallery/{kind}/{id}/thumb` and `.../header`.

id.description:
The asset key the scripts name, lowercased (`avg_1_1`, `bg_corridor`):
what a profile background stores.

width.description: The source PNG's size in px.

StoryAssets.description:
The assets one script references, keyed by the raw name as written in the
script (`avg_225_haak_1#3$1`, `$escape_loop`). Only resolved names appear.

avatars.description:
`[popupdialog]` head portraits, keyed by the raw `dialoghead` value
(`$avatar_amiya`). 163 distinct values over EN, all 163 resolve.

imageSizes.description:
Every name in `backgrounds` and `images`, under the SAME key, with the
plate metrics that size it when the command carries no `screenadapt`.

videos.description:
Cutscene clips, keyed by the `[Video]` command's own `res` argument
(`video/act38side/PV01.mp4`) so the engine looks a halt up by the
string it already holds. Only resolved references appear: 12 of the 25
distinct names the EN scripts reference have a file, the other 13 are
clips EN retired and the reader skips them.

StoryCommand.description:
One parsed line. `kind` is lowercased and typo-normalised; a bare text line
is `kind: "text"` with the whole line in `text`.

line.description: 1-based line number in the script file.

StoryCommunity.description: The community reading aggregate for one server.

computedAt.description: Unix seconds this aggregate was computed at.

groups.description:
Every group in the library index, the operator record groups included,
in index order.

players.description:
Accounts counted: those that passed the privacy gate and carry at least
one of the three sources. It is the denominator for every count here.

stories.description: Every story in the library index, in index order.

StoryCoverKind.description:
Where a group's `coverUrl` came from. `EntryPic` is the game's own
Archives picture; `Background` is DERIVED, the first background of the
group's first scripted story, because most EN groups have no
`StoryEntryPicId` and all 17 mainline chapters are among them.

code.description: The operation code (`GT-1`), absent on records and interludes.

hasScript.description:
True when a script file answers the probe, so `GET /story/{id}` will
return a script rather than a 404.

hasVideo.description:
The script plays a `[Video]`. 1 of the 1,797 scripted EN stories is
nothing but one (`main_14_level_main_14-20_beg`).

wordCount.description:
Whitespace-separated words of prose in the script, counted once at
index build by the same rule as `StoryScript.wordCount`. 0 when the
story has no script.

StoryGallery.description:
`GET /story/gallery`: every Archives gallery picture, by the archive that
lists it.

bannerUrl.description:
The group's KEY VISUAL, `StorylineStorySets[].KvImageId` resolved
through `spritepack/mixstory_kv_sprites_{0,1,2}`: the card art the
game's own Story Collection draws. It is NOT `coverUrl`: a cover is the
Archives entry picture (67 groups) or a derived first background (382),
while a banner is the authored 532x456 plate and exists for exactly the
81 groups a storyline shelf lists, all 17 mainline chapters among them.
For an event both exist and differ; the banner is the key visual.

chapterNumber.description:
0 through 16 on the 17 mainline chapters, absent everywhere else. Read
off the ZONE (`zone_table.ZoneNameTitleCurrent`, the "00".."16" the
client prints under `EPISODE`), falling back to the `main_N` id. It is
what a reader actually knows a chapter by, where `name` is an arc
title nobody remembers.

oneOf.description: Which source `coverUrl` came from, absent exactly when `coverUrl` is.

displayType.description:
`activity_table.BasicInfo.DisplayType` for event groups (`SIDESTORY`,
`BRANCHLINE`, `MINISTORY`, `NONE`); the game's own Archives shelf.

iconUrl.description:
The group's own small glyph, `MainlineData.DecoImageId` resolved
through `spritepack/mixstory_deco_sprites_h2_0`. MAINLINE only: the
table carries a deco for the 17 chapters and for nothing else, so an
event group has none and the UI falls back to its title or code.

illustrationCount.description:
Distinct backgrounds plus distinct CGs the group's scripts reference,
the row count of the ILLUSTRATIONS tab. Counted over names, resolved
or not.

oneOf.description:
The group's THEME, the track the game plays over its Archives entry:
`music_3in1bg_main{N}` on a mainline chapter and the
`sys.ON_ACTIVITY_LOADED.{id}` bank on an event. 86 of the 87 EN
library groups carry one and 6 of those carry a title; the one that
does not is `act24side`, whose bank names a loop clip the tree does
not hold.

spriteCount.description:
Distinct sprite folders the group's scripts reference, the row count
of the Sprites sub-tab.

startTime.description:
Unix release time, `-1` when nothing dates the group. It is the
group's own `StartTime`, except on a MAINLINE group, where every one of
the 17 EN rows writes -1 and the date is the zone's
`zone_table.MainlineAdditionInfo.ZoneOpenTime` instead (5 of 17 carry
one: `main_10` 1666180800 through `main_14` 1730394000). No field says
which source answered, because a release date is a release date and the
consumer renders one line either way.

titleImageUrl.description:
The group's title as ART, `StorylineStorySets[].TitleImageId` resolved
through `spritepack/mixstory_title_sprites_0`: the 516x260 logotype the
game sets behind the written title, on all 81 groups a storyline shelf
lists. It carries the same words as `name`, drawn, so a consumer that
shows it still prints `name` for search and for a reader who cannot see
the image.

wordCount.description: The sum of this group's stories' `wordCount`.

StoryGroupReaders.description: One group, its readers, its finishers and its depth curve.

depth.description:
Readers per story, in the group's own story order: the "how far people
get" curve. It is the same number `stories[]` carries for each id,
arranged so a consumer can draw the curve without a join.

ABSENT on an operator's records, and only there. Carrying it for all
766 groups put the document at 153,950 bytes, over the 150 KB the wire
contract allows; dropping it from the 315 record groups, which hold 367
one-story-deep curves that say nothing their `readers` count does not,
brings it to 150,066. That is 3,534 bytes under the ceiling and about 70
more stories, which is a THIN margin: the real-data test asserts the
ceiling, so the next EN batch that crosses it says so before the wire
does, and the fix then is to drop the curve everywhere and let the
consumer join it. A consumer that wants a record's curve reads
`stories[]`, which is where every one of these numbers came from.

finished.description:
Accounts that have read every GATED story in the group, the stories
the stage records can speak for. A group with no gated story counts 0,
and the tab prints that as not measurable rather than as nobody:
494 EN stories carry no gate (every operator record, 20 mini vignettes,
`main_0`'s two Prologue guide entries), and 2,313 of 2,576 accounts are
known only through their stage records, so "every scripted story"
would have made chapter 0 finished by 0 of its 2,314 readers.

id.description:
A `StoryGroup.id` (`main_8`, `act17side`) or, for an operator's
records, that operator's `charId`.

readers.description: Accounts that have read at least one story in the group.

StoryIllustrations.description:
Every illustration one group or one operator's records reference, in
first-appearance order over the group's stories in library order.

groupId.description: The id as asked for: a `StoryGroup.id` or an operator `charId`.

storylines.description:
The game's themed shelves, in `SortId` order. Empty when the loaded
`stage_table` carries no `Storylines` (every CN/EN tree since 2024
does).

StoryMusic.description:
The theme a story group plays, resolved to clips.

`loopUrl` is the only required half: 59 of the 86 EN groups that have a
theme also carry a one-shot `introUrl` in front of it, and a group whose
loop clip is not on disk carries no `music` at all rather than a URL that
404s. `title` is the `Musics` row's `Name`, which 101 of the 208 EN rows
write as a single space, so it is trimmed and dropped when empty.

StoryProgressDocument.description:
The reading-progress document, exactly as the browser holds it.

Opaque on purpose: typing it here would put the format in two places and
make every reader-side field addition a backend migration. The TS type is
declared inline so the generated binding still names the real shape.

gameArchived.description:
How many of `game_read` the game's ARCHIVE lists. The rest are known
only from the client's played-script flags, which is the half that
covers the mainline.

gameRead.description:
Story ids the GAME says this account has read, imported on the last
game-data refresh. Empty when the account has never refreshed, or when
the payload carried no story block.

gameSyncedAt.description: Unix seconds of that import, null when nothing has ever been imported.

gameUnread.description:
Story ids the game's Archive lists that NOTHING played: unlocked by an
event, never opened. A v1 document may carry these as read marks,
because the first import baked its whole union into the document; the
client's v1 -> v2 upgrade withdraws exactly these and nothing else.

oneOf.description: The stored document, or null when this account has never synced.

updatedAt.description: Unix seconds of the last write, null alongside a null `progress`.

StoryReaders.description: One story and how many accounts have read it.

StoryScript.description: One story, parsed, with every asset it references resolved.

synopsis.description:
The game's own "story summary" for this story, the text its Skip
dialog shows: the `[uc]info` file `StoryInfo` names, trimmed. Absent
when the table names none or the file is not on disk. It rides the
SCRIPT response and not the library index, because the index would
carry all 1,881 of them on every library load.

StorySpriteDetail.description:
One sprite folder's expression sheet: its list entry, every expression
it offers, and every story it appears in, in library order.

names.description:
The kept names of `sprite.names`, in the same order, each with where it
is spoken and example lines.

strayNames.description:
The names the alias threshold CUT (`sprite.noise` is their weight),
most lines first, with the same detail: mostly someone else speaking
while this sprite stays lit. Never searched and never a chip of their
own; the sheet lists them behind a disclosure.

StorySpriteEntry.description:
One sprite folder in the gallery list: who it is, what the scripts call
it, how much it speaks, and the one expression its card shows.

base.description: The folder under `textures/avg/characters/`, as spelled on disk.

firstOrder.description: That story's position in library order, for a stable sort.

firstSeen.description:
The earliest `startTime` (unix seconds) of a group that shows it,
counting only dated groups; mainline groups carry none.

firstStory.description: The first story, in library order, that shows it.

lines.description: Weighted named lines attributed to this sprite over the library.

names.description:
The names the scripts speak this sprite under, most lines first. Empty
when no named line was ever attributed to it. Only ALIASES are listed:
a name needs 3 weighted lines and 2% of the folder's named lines, the
primary excepted; what the cut drops is `noise`.

noise.description:
Weighted named lines whose names fell under the alias threshold:
mostly someone else speaking while this sprite stays lit.

storyCount.description: Distinct library stories that put this sprite up.

oneOf.description: The expression the card shows: the most used one, else the first.

variant.description:
What the folder adds after the `char_*` id: the set number (`1`) or
an outfit tag (`ex`). Never part of the name.

variantCount.description: How many distinct expressions the folder offers.

StorySpriteExample.description:
One line spoken under a name while the sprite is lit. `line` is the
script's own line (`StoryCommand.line`), which the reader resolves to a
halt with `?line=`; `text` is as written, rich-text tags and
`{@nickname}` intact.

StorySpriteIndex.description: Every story sprite folder, one entry each, in folder-name order.

StorySpriteKind.description: Whether a sprite folder draws an operator or a member of the cast.

StorySpriteName.description:
One display name the scripts speak a sprite under, and how many lines.
`count` is WEIGHTED: a line with two lit sprites counts half for each, so
it is a number with at most two decimals rather than an integer.

StorySpriteNameDetail.description:
One kept name of a sprite folder, for the sheet's name popover: its
weighted lines, the stories that use it (most lines first, at most 5, and
how many more), and up to 3 example lines, spread over different stories
where the name is spoken in more than one.

StorySpriteNameStory.description: One story that speaks a sprite under one name.

lines.description: Weighted lines under this name in this story.

StorySpriteStory.description: One story a sprite appears in, with the lines attributed to it there.

lines.description:
Weighted named lines attributed to the sprite in this story; 0 when
it is on stage but never the speaker.

tag.description:
The story's `avgTag` ("Before Operation", "After Operation"), which
tells apart the two halves of one stage that share a name.

uses.description: How often the story puts the sprite up.

StorySpriteVariant.description:
One expression a sprite folder OFFERS: a `#N$M` key and the files it
resolves to, by the same resolver `GET /story/{id}` uses. Two keys that
land on the same body and face are one expression, listed under the first
key that reaches it. `wholeBody` is true when no face patch is composited:
the body plate IS the expression (a legacy whole sprite, or a hub entry
flagged `isWholeBody`). `uses` counts how often the scripts PUT this
expression up (a slot, a cut-in, a window).

StoryTotals.description:
The library's size, over the DISTINCT story ids in the index: the 364
`record` groups and the 315 operator records list the same 367 stories,
so a naive sum of both halves would count those twice.

StoryZone.description: A main chapter's names, from `zone_table` and `chapter_table`.

Storyline.description:
One of the game's own themed shelves over the Archives
(`stage_table.Storylines`), with the `StoryGroup.id`s it holds, in the
order the shelf lists them.

The join is `StorylineStorySets`, NOT the group id: a location names a
`RelevantStorySetId`, that set is `MAINLINE` and names a zone
(`MainlineData.ZoneId`, which is the mainline group's own id) or `SS` /
`COLLECT` and names an activity (`RelevantActivityId`, which is the event
group's own id). On EN 81 of 81 sets resolve and 79 of them name a group
the Archives list; the other 2 (`setId_mainline_3_1` -> `act2mainss`,
`setId_mainline_3_2` -> `act3mainss`) name ids `story_review_table` does
not carry and are dropped.

A group can sit on SEVERAL shelves (17 do on EN), so `groupIds` over all
storylines is not a partition: it lists 104 slots over 81 distinct groups.
Picking one shelf per group is the consumer's job.

oneOf.description:
The mainline chapters this shelf spans: the min and max
`StoryGroup.chapterNumber` over its groups. `mainLine` is 0 to 16, and
a themed shelf carries one when it holds mainline chapters of its own
(`ssLine_1` holds `main_7` through `main_14`); it is absent on the 7 EN
shelves that hold none.

iconUrl.description:
The shelf's own glyph: `StorylineIconId`
(`spritepack/mixstory_abbr_sprites_h2_0`, 44x36, 13 of the 14 EN
shelves) and, where that is absent, `StorylineLogoId`
(`spritepack/mixstory_logo_sprites_0`, 14 of 14). `mainLine` is the one
shelf with no abbreviation glyph, so it draws its logo.

logoUrl.description:
The shelf's LOGO, `StorylineLogoId` (`spritepack/mixstory_logo_sprites_0`,
108x108, 14 of 14 EN shelves): the emblem the game's Story Collection
draws for the shelf, monochrome white on transparent. The jump bar draws
this so every shelf chip carries the same kind of mark as the arcs.

StorylineArc.description:
One arc inside a storyline: the run of groups between two of the game's
own `MAINLINE_SPLIT` headers. Only `mainLine` carries any on EN (4:
`HOUR OF AN AWAKENING`, `SHATTER OF A VISION`, `SHADOW OF A DYING SUN`,
`NEXUS POINT OF FUTURE`); every `ssLine_*` has an empty list.

oneOf.description:
The chapters the arc spans: the min and max
`StoryGroup.chapterNumber` over the groups on it that carry one.
Absent on an arc that holds no numbered chapter at all.

iconUrl.description:
The arc header's own icon, `MainlineSplitData.IconId` resolved through
`spritepack/mixstory_deco_sprites_h2_0` (`act_0` to `act_3`, 184x52).
All 4 EN mainline arcs carry one and nothing else declares an arc.

SupportUnit.description: One entry in a Doctor's published support roster (slot 0..2).

elite.description:
Joined from `user_operators` - null if the support refers to an op the
player no longer owns (shouldn't happen, but the FK is soft).

SustainEntryDto.description:
One operator's endurance in the room the draft puts them in. Drain is the
game's own per-hour figure (including the operator's own morale-cost riders),
not a per-room approximation.

lasts_hours.description:
Hours until empty FROM THE CURRENT BAR when the sync knows it, else
from full. `None` = never depletes.

morale.description:
The operator's morale as of the last account sync (0-24). Absent when
the sync doesn't cover them.

SustainabilityDto.description:
The rotation validated by a time-stepped morale simulation (game-true drain
and dorm-recovery rates): honest evidence the plan survives its own rhythm,
instead of an unchecked recommendation.

depleted.description: Operators whose morale empties while working, with when and where.

dorm_overflow.description: Peak number of resting operators the dorms could not hold at once.

facilities.description:
Per-facility simulated totals over the horizon, with lost hours (dark
shifts + post-depletion time). Absent on older payloads.

timeline.description:
Every simulated operator's morale over the week, sampled at 12h block
boundaries - the "morale over time" chart. Most-at-risk first.

verdict.description: "`holds_up`" - nobody runs dry; "depletes" - someone's morale hits zero mid-shift.

entity_kinds.description:
The kinds the list's editor offers. Lists cached or snapshotted before
the column existed read as operator-only, which is what they were.

entity_id.description: Was `operator_id`; old snapshots still spell it that way.

entity_kind.description:
Absent from snapshots and cache entries written before kinds existed,
all of which were operators.

TrainerHintDto.description: One trainer suggestion for the declared training class.

value_pct.description: Specialization training speed % their best matching skill provides.

TranslationEntry.description:
One row of the translation editor: the key and its English source joined to
this locale's translation, if any.

`is_stale` is computed in SQL rather than stored - it is true when a
translation exists but was written against an older English source, which
is the only staleness this system has.

`translated_source_text` is the English that was on screen when the value
was saved. It is what turns `is_stale` from a badge into a diff, and it is
`None` for rows saved before the snapshot column existed.

TranslationPermission.description: `translation_permissions` row. Shape-identical to a tier-list permission.

UiMessageAuditEntry.description:
Per-key/locale history. `old_value` is what makes revert a write rather
than a restore.

UpdateGroupRequest.description: A group update. Give at least one field; an absent one keeps its value.

entity_kinds.description:
The kinds the list's editor offers, in pool tab order. Omitted keeps
the stored set; an empty set is a 400. Dropping a kind leaves every
placement of it on the list: the set is what the pool offers, not what
the list may hold.

oneOf.description:
Absent leaves the saved layout alone, `null` resets it to the default
(today's order, every tab visible, no showcase, no background). An
object sets the keys it carries and keeps the rest: `tabs` replaces the
tab list, `showcase` the blocks, `background` the header art (`null`
removes it). Normalized before it is stored: unknown tab ids and
repeats are dropped, missing tabs appended visible.

public_profile.description:
Each flag: absent leaves it as stored, so a caller can send only the
field it changes (the profile's tab editor sends only `profile_layout`).

UserCheckin.description:
`user_checkin` table: daily sign-in state from the game's `checkIn` section,
joined with the timestamps needed to render it as a calendar.

The game's monthly sign-in is a *sequential list of reward slots*, not a
dated calendar: missing a day leaves you one slot behind, it never forfeits
the slot. Nothing in this payload maps a claim to the date it happened on,
so no consumer can say "the 4th was missed", only "N of the month's slots
are claimed, D days have elapsed".

can_check_in.description: Whether a daily sign-in is claimable right now (as of the last sync).

claimed_this_month.description:
Sign-ins claimed in the current month's series: the length of
`monthly_card_flags`, derived in SQL so no client re-derives it.

cumulative_signin.description: Lifetime cumulative sign-in days (the "total days of sign-ins" counter).

last_online_ts.description:
Player's last in-game online time (Unix seconds), distinct from the DB
sync time below.

monthly_card_flags.description:
One flag per sign-in **claimed** this month, in claim order: `1` if the
monthly-subscription Daily Supply came with that claim, `0` if not.

This is the game's raw `checkInHistory`, and it is **not** a per-day
calendar: a missed day produces no entry at all. Reading `flags[d - 1]`
as "day `d` was claimed" is wrong, and counting the `1`s counts monthly
card days, not sign-ins. (Verified against `user_status.monthly_sub_end`
over the whole user table: the final flag agrees with subscription state
in 2 193 of 2 219 non-empty rows.) Use [`Self::claimed_this_month`] for
the sign-in count.

register_ts.description: Account creation time (Unix seconds), for "days since joining".

reward_index.description:
The game's raw `checkInRewardIndex`: a 0-based pointer into the month's
reward slots. It equals `claimed_this_month` while a claim is pending
and `claimed_this_month - 1` just after one, and a handful of rows carry
a stale `0` across a series rollover. Prefer `claimed_this_month`.

updated_at.description:
When this row was last synced to our DB. Every field above is a snapshot
as of this moment, which may be days/weeks before "now", so the month
the calendar belongs to is this timestamp's month, not today's.

originite.description: Originite Prime on the account (paid and free pools summed) as of the last sync.

oneOf.description:
The owner's tab order and visibility, normalized on read. `None` when
they never customized, which the client renders exactly as before
layouts existed. A visitor receives [`UserProfile::hide_private_tabs`]'s
projection, which lists only the visible tabs.

base_infrastructure.description:
The base grade's infrastructure-completeness component (built rooms vs
the same rooms at max level). None on pre-split rows.

base_utilization.description:
The base grade's stationing-utilization component (actual vs the
optimizer's best on the built rooms). None on rows graded before the
split was stored.

VerifySession.description:
The `/auth/verify` response: the session a token currently represents.

Serialized directly by the handler, so this declaration is the wire format,
the `OpenAPI` schema and the generated TypeScript at once.

canAccessAdminPanel.description:
True for a role that may open the admin panel, or for any holder of a
translation grant.

role.description:
Re-read from the database on every call, so a promotion takes effect
without the user logging out and back in.

server.description: The game server the session is bound to.

valid.description: Always true - a failing token is a 401, not `valid: false`.

VideoSources.description:
The two transcodes of one cutscene clip. `webm` is offered first and `mp4`
is the fallback; a clip is only ever missing one of them when a transcode
failed, since the unpacker's video step (`backfill-video`, and the tail of
every `extract`) writes both.

ViewRecorded.description:
Whether a `POST /tier-lists/{slug}/view` counted as a new view.

Serialized directly by the handler, so this declaration is the wire format,
the `OpenAPI` schema and the generated TypeScript at once.

unique.description: False when the same user or session already counted for this list.

VisibilityState.description:
Whether a tier list appears in the public index.

Hiding a list does not make it private: a direct link still resolves.

BadRequest.description: The request body or query string was malformed.

Conflict.description: The write collides with something already stored, such as a group name that is already taken.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated, but not permitted to read or modify this resource. Reading another player's data returns this when their profile is private.

RateLimited.description: Rate limit exceeded. The limit is per-IP and applies across the whole API.

ServiceUnavailable.description: The server is shedding load (CPU admission control or database backpressure). The request is safe to retry.

Unauthorized.description: No credentials were supplied, or the bearer token is expired or invalid.

ValidationFailed.description: The body was well-formed but failed validation; `error.details` lists the offending fields.

bearer_auth.description: A site token from one of the `/api/login*` endpoints. Valid for seven days.

service_key.name: x-service-key
service_key.description: Internal shared secret for server-side rendering. Not issued to third parties.
